newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares slip at open,eyes on Wong's debut.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares slip at open,eyes on Wong's debut.

text.p: The Singapore stock market slipped early Thursday after the Dow's sharp fall overnight but dealers said the downside was limited as trade was thin

They said the focus was on newly-listed Wong's Circuits, which topped the actives with over 13 million shares. The shares shot to a high of US$1.14 in early trade against its initial public offer of US$0.88. It was at US$1.03 in mid morning.
After opening flat at 2,192.14, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index eased 10.62 points to 2,181.83 at 0215 GMT.
Turnover was light around 31 million shares, with losers leading gainers by 108 to 27.

Precision engineering company Uraco Holdings was active with 1.6 million shares. Managing director Lim Ee Ann told Reuters he was not involved in this morning's sales. Lim had recently sold 15 million shares for Singapore $13.3 million (US$9.5 million) to finance "a personal investment".
Multimedia company Creative Technology led gainers, rising Singapore $0.20 to S$13.70 on 95,600 shares.
Profit-taking by foreign institutions dampened foreign tranches of Singapore Press Holdings (SPH) and banks like DBS and OUB. SPH fell S$0.40 to S$26.50 and DBS fell S$0.30 to S$18.40.
